In @bib{RN2720@623}, three different vowel classes are considered possible for @i{mašālu}, depending on the dialect (@i{u/u} for OB/SB, @i{a/a} for SB and @i{i/i} for MB). Therefore, the vowel in the preterite form does not seem to be a sufficient reason to determine the correct reading of the verb. The verb @i{mašālu} is favored here because it fits the overall structure of the passage: the verb at the end of this line is connected to the prepositions @i{kīma}/@i{kī} (l. 12) and @i{ana} (l. 21), and both of these prepositions can be used with @i{mašālu} to indicate the object of resemblance (see @bib{RN2721@M/1 355-356}). See also the discussion in @bib{RN1402@66}.
